text.en: In Ainu oral literature, the inflectional prefix *i-* functions as the first-person objective marker, and the use of this first-person singular or plural object prefix is restricted to oral literature ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-use-of-the-first-person-singular-plural⟧⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-ainu-oral-literature-the-inflectional-prefix-i⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語の口承文芸において、屈折接頭辞 *i-* は1人称目的格標識として機能し、この1人称単数または複数目的語接頭辞の使用は口承文芸に制限される⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-use-of-the-first-person-singular-plural⟧⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-ainu-oral-literature-the-inflectional-prefix-i⟧。

text.en: First-person singular verbal agreement exhibits a nominative/accusative alignment, marking subjects (A and S) with *ku=* and objects (O) with *en=*, contrasting with second-person verbal agreement, which follows a neutral alignment without distinction between A, S, and O, marking the singular with *e=* and the plural with *eci=* ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--second-person-neutral-alignment⟧⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--first-person-singular-nom-acc-alignment⟧. In the Saru dialect, the first-person singular has the pronoun *káni*, the nominative affix *ku-*, and the objective affix *'en-*, which has singular grammatical number and refers to the speaker ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-first-person-singular-has-the-pronoun-k⟧. Also in the Saru dialect, the first-person singular subject is marked by *ku-* across one-, two-, and three-argument verbs, and the first-person singular object is marked by *en-* ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-the-saru-dialect-first-person-singular-subject⟧. Correspondingly, in the Saru dialect, the second-person singular is marked by *e-* for both subjects across one-, two-, and three-argument verbs and objects, and the second-person plural is marked by *eci-* for both subjects and objects ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-the-saru-dialect-second-person-singular-is⟧. In the Shizunai dialect, in combined nominative-objective forms, the first-person nominative is always realized as *a-* or *an-*, identical to the indefinite pronominal affix ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-combined-nominative-objective-forms-in-the-shizunai⟧. In the classical language, a second-person subject acting on a first-person object is marked by prefixing *e-i-* for a singular subject or *echi-i-* for a plural subject to the verb ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-the-classical-language-a-second-person-subject⟧. In Classical Ainu, second-person and third-person zero subject marking are the same for both intransitive and transitive verbs ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-classical-ainu-second-person-and-third-person⟧. In Classical Ainu, the first-person singular intransitive verb suffix *-an* retains its vowel *a* even when the stem vowel is *o*, as in *hosipi-an* 'I returned' ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-classical-ainu-the-first-person-singular-intransitive⟧.
text.ja: 1人称単数の動詞一致は主格・対格型アラインメントを示して主語（AおよびS）を *ku=* で、目的語（O）を *en=* で標示するが、これとは対照的に、2人称の動詞一致はA・S・Oの区別のない中立型アラインメントに従い、単数を *e=*、複数を *eci=* で標示する⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--second-person-neutral-alignment⟧⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--first-person-singular-nom-acc-alignment⟧。沙流方言において、1人称単数は代名詞 *káni*、主格接辞 *ku-*、目的格接辞 *'en-* をもち、文法上の数は単数で話し手自身を指す⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-first-person-singular-has-the-pronoun-k⟧。同じく沙流方言では、1人称単数主語は1項・2項・3項動詞を通じて *ku-* で標示され、1人称単数目的語は *en-* で標示される⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-the-saru-dialect-first-person-singular-subject⟧。また沙流方言において、2人称単数は1項・2項・3項動詞の主語および目的語の双方で *e-* によって標示され、2人称複数も主語および目的語の双方で *eci-* によって標示される⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-the-saru-dialect-second-person-singular-is⟧。静内方言の主格・目的格結合形において、1人称主格は常に不定称代名接辞と同一の *a-* または *an-* として実現される⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-combined-nominative-objective-forms-in-the-shizunai⟧。雅語においては、2人称主格から1人称目的格への作用は、単数主語では接頭辞 *e-i-*、複数主語では *echi-i-* を動詞に前置して標示される⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-the-classical-language-a-second-person-subject⟧。古典アイヌ語では、2人称および3人称（ゼロ）の主語標示は自動詞と他動詞の双方で同一である⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-classical-ainu-second-person-and-third-person⟧。古典アイヌ語において、自動詞の1人称単数接尾辞 *-an* は、*hosipi-an*「私は戻った」のように語幹母音が *o* である場合でも一貫して母音 *a* を保つ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-classical-ainu-the-first-person-singular-intransitive⟧。

text.en: The first-person singular subjective personal affix is *ku-* ~ *k-* ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-first-person-singular-subjective-personal-affix-is⟧. These subject personal affixes *k-* and *ku-* cannot stand as independent words and must be placed immediately preceding the verb ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--subject-personal-affixes-k-and-ku-cannot-stand⟧. The affix takes the form *k-* before vowel-initial verbs and *ku-* before consonant-initial verbs ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-first-person-singular-subjective-personal-affix-takes⟧, specifically appearing as *ku-* before consonants and as *k-* before vowels except *i* ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-first-person-singular-subjective-prefix-ku-is⟧. In colloquial Ainu, the first-person singular transitive verb prefix *ku-* is not affected by the stem vowel, as in *ku-kor* 'I have' ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-colloquial-ainu-the-first-person-singular-transitive⟧. In the colloquial subjective conjugation of Class I verbs, the first-person singular is *ku-*, the first-person plural exclusive is *chi-*, and the first-person plural inclusive is *a-* ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-the-colloquial-subjective-conjugation-of-class-i-2⟧, and more generally in Colloquial Ainu, the first-person transitive subject markers are *ku-* for singular, *ci-* for exclusive plural, and *a-* (*an-*) for inclusive plural ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-colloquial-ainu-the-first-person-transitive-subject⟧. In Southern Hokkaido, the prefix *ku=* (first-person singular A/S) loses its vowel */u/* before a vowel-initial verb stem (*/a, e, o, u/*), becoming *k=* ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-southern-hokkaido-the-prefix-ku-first-person⟧. In Western Hidaka and Chitose dialects, before verb stems beginning with *a*, *u*, *e*, or *o*, the vowel *u* of the first-person singular subject prefix *k(u)=* drops, and *k* fuses with the initial syllable ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-western-hidaka-and-chitose-dialects-before-verb⟧. In the Saru dialect, the person affixes *ku=* 'I' and *ci=* 'we' lose their vowels */u/* and */i/* respectively before words beginning with */a, u, e, o/* ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-the-saru-dialect-the-person-affixes-ku⟧. In the Saru dialect, when quoting one's own speech, the quotative first person is not used, and regular first-person forms such as *káni* and *ku-* are retained ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--when-quoting-one-s-own-speech-the-quotative⟧. In the Shizunai dialect, the first-person singular nominative is marked by the prefix *ku-* ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--shizunai-first-person-singular-nominative-ku⟧. This prefix *ku-* in the Shizunai dialect never occurs in *yukar* epics, belongs strictly to everyday colloquial speech ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--shizunai-ku-absent-from-yukar⟧, is restricted to a personal and concrete first person, and is avoided in quotations and pretended first-person contexts in favor of the indefinite person ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--shizunai-ku-concrete-personal-restriction⟧. In Sakhalin Ainu elder speech, the youth speech first-person plural affix *'an=*/*='an* is used as the first-person singular personal affix instead of *ku=* ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-sakhalin-ainu-elder-speech-uses-the-youth⟧.
text.ja: 1人称単数主格の人称接辞は *ku-* 〜 *k-* である⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-first-person-singular-subjective-personal-affix-is⟧。主格人称接辞 *k-* および *ku-* は自立語として単独で用いることはできず、必ず動詞の直前に置かれなければならない⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--subject-personal-affixes-k-and-ku-cannot-stand⟧。この接辞は母音で始まる動詞の前では *k-*、子音で始まる動詞の前では *ku-* となり⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-first-person-singular-subjective-personal-affix-takes⟧、より特定的に子音の前では *ku-* が、*i* を除く母音の前では *k-* が用いられる⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-first-person-singular-subjective-prefix-ku-is⟧。口語アイヌ語において、他動詞の1人称単数接頭辞 *ku-* は、*ku-kor*「私は持っている」のように語幹母音の影響を受けない⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-colloquial-ainu-the-first-person-singular-transitive⟧。第I類動詞の口語主格活用において、1人称単数は *ku-*、1人称複数除外は *chi-*、包括は *a-* であり⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-the-colloquial-subjective-conjugation-of-class-i-2⟧、口語アイヌ語一般において1人称他動詞主語標識は単数で *ku-*、排他複数で *ci-*、包括複数で *a-* (*an-*) である⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-colloquial-ainu-the-first-person-transitive-subject⟧。北海道南部方言において、1人称単数A/S接頭辞 *ku=* は母音（*/a, e, o, u/*）で始まる動詞語幹の前で母音 */u/* が脱落して *k=* となる⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-southern-hokkaido-the-prefix-ku-first-person⟧。日高西部・千歳方言では、*a*, *u*, *e*, *o* で始まる語幹の前で1人称単数主格接頭辞 *k(u)=* の *u* が脱落し、*k* のみが後続音節と融合する⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-western-hidaka-and-chitose-dialects-before-verb⟧。沙流方言において、人称接辞 *ku=*「私が」および *ci=*「私たちが」は、*/a, u, e, o/* で始まる単語の前でそれぞれ母音 */u/* および */i/* が脱落する⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-the-saru-dialect-the-person-affixes-ku⟧。沙流方言で自分の発話を引用する場合、引用の1人称にはならず、*káni* や *ku-* などの通常の1人称形式が維持される⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--when-quoting-one-s-own-speech-the-quotative⟧。静内方言において、1人称単数主格は接頭辞 *ku-* によって標示される⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--shizunai-first-person-singular-nominative-ku⟧。静内方言の接頭辞 *ku-* はユーカラ叙事詩には決して現れずもっぱら日常口語に属し⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--shizunai-ku-absent-from-yukar⟧、その用法は個人的かつ具体的な1人称に限定され、引用や仮構の1人称文脈では回避されて代わりに不定人称が用いられる⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--shizunai-ku-concrete-personal-restriction⟧。樺太アイヌ語の老人言葉では、1人称単数の人称接辞として若者言葉の *ku=* ではなく、若者言葉の1人称複数形 *'an=*/*='an* が用いられる⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-sakhalin-ainu-elder-speech-uses-the-youth⟧。

text.en: In the spoken language, the first-person singular object of a transitive verb is marked by the prefix *en-* ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-the-spoken-language-the-first-person-singular⟧. The first-person singular objective personal affix is *en-* ('me / to me'), distinct in form from the subjective *ku-* or *k-* ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-first-person-singular-objective-personal-affix-is⟧⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-first-person-singular-objective-personal-affix-is-2⟧⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-first-person-singular-objective-person-affix-is⟧. In Colloquial Ainu, the first-person object markers are *en-* for singular, *un-* for exclusive plural, and *i-* for inclusive plural ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-colloquial-ainu-the-first-person-object-markers⟧. The prefix *i-* also marks the first-person singular objective ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-prefix-i-marks-the-first-person-singular⟧. The objective prefix *en-* basically means 'me' in the accusative, but when used with ditransitive verbs of giving such as *kore* 'give', it corresponds to or is translated as the dative 'to me' ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-first-person-singular-objective-prefix-en-means⟧⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-objective-person-prefix-en-basically-means-me⟧. In colloquial speech in Hokkaido, the combination of a second-person singular subject with a first-person singular object is not **e-en-* but *en-*, with the second-person singular subject prefix *e-* not appearing, a characteristic also shared by the elevated or poetic language ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-colloquial-speech-the-second-person-singular-subject⟧. In the Chitose dialect, an action from a second-person singular or plural subject to a first-person singular object is expressed solely by *en-*, lacking an overt second-person subject prefix and thus not forming **e-en-* or **eci-en-* ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-chitose-ainu-an-action-from-second-person⟧. In Chitose Ainu, the poetic or elevated first-person object personal affix meaning 'you to me' as a combined subject/object marker is *i-* ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-chitose-ainu-the-poetic-elevated-first-person⟧. In the Saru and Chitose dialects, the combination of a second-person singular subject and a first-person object is expressed as *en=* for a singular object and *un=* for a plural object, identical to the forms for a third-person subject with a first-person object, rather than *e=en=* and *e=un=* as found in other dialects ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-saru-and-chitose-dialects-the-combination-of⟧. In the Shizunai dialect, the first-person singular objective is marked by the prefix *en-* ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--shizunai-first-person-singular-objective-en⟧, which belongs exclusively to colloquial language and is restricted to concrete, personal reference ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--shizunai-en-colloquial-concrete-restriction⟧. In the Sakhalin dialect, *in-* functions as a first-person objective prefix ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-the-sakhalin-dialect-in-functions-as-a⟧.
text.ja: 口語において、他動詞の第1人称単数目的格は接頭辞 *en-* で示される⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-the-spoken-language-the-first-person-singular⟧。1人称単数の目的格人称接辞は *en-*（「私を」「私に」）であり、主格の *ku-*（または *k-*）とは形態が異なる⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-first-person-singular-objective-personal-affix-is⟧⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-first-person-singular-objective-personal-affix-is-2⟧⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-first-person-singular-objective-person-affix-is⟧。口語アイヌ語において、1人称目的語標識は単数で *en-*、排他複数で *un-*、包括複数で *i-* である⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-colloquial-ainu-the-first-person-object-markers⟧。接頭辞 *i-* もまた1人称単数目的格を表す⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-prefix-i-marks-the-first-person-singular⟧。目的格接頭辞 *en-* は基本的に対格「私を」を意味するが、*kore*「与える」のような授与動詞とともに用いられると与格「私に」に対応する⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-first-person-singular-objective-prefix-en-means⟧⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-objective-person-prefix-en-basically-means-me⟧。北海道の口語において、2人称単数主格と1人称単数目的格の組み合わせは **e-en-* ではなく *en-* となり、2人称単数主格の接頭辞 *e-* は現れず、雅語もこの特徴を共有する⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-colloquial-speech-the-second-person-singular-subject⟧。千歳方言において、2人称単数または2人称複数から1人称単数への行為は *en-* のみで示され、表層の2人称主格接頭辞を欠いて **e-en-* や **eci-en-* にはならない⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-chitose-ainu-an-action-from-second-person⟧。また千歳方言では、「お前が私を／に」を意味する主格・目的格結合の雅語人称接辞は *i-* である⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-chitose-ainu-the-poetic-elevated-first-person⟧。沙流・千歳方言では、2人称単数主格と1人称目的格の組み合わせにおいて、他方言で *e=en=*、*e=un=* となるところを、3人称主格と1人称目的格の組み合わせと同じ *en=*（単数目的語）および *un=*（複数目的語）で標示する⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-saru-and-chitose-dialects-the-combination-of⟧。静内方言において、1人称単数目的格は接頭辞 *en-* によって標示され⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--shizunai-first-person-singular-objective-en⟧、これは排他的に口語に属して具体的・個人的な参照に限定される⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--shizunai-en-colloquial-concrete-restriction⟧。樺太方言では、*in-* が1人称目的格接頭辞として機能する⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-the-sakhalin-dialect-in-functions-as-a⟧。

text.en: The second-person singular subjective personal affix is *e-* ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-second-person-singular-subjective-personal-affix-is⟧, and the second-person singular objective personal affix is likewise *e-* ('you sg.') ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-second-person-singular-objective-personal-affix-is⟧⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-second-person-singular-objective-person-affix-is⟧. Second-person personal affixes show no morphological distinction between subjective and objective case, appearing as *e-* for singular and *eci-* for plural in both roles ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--second-person-affixes-have-no-morphological-distinction-between⟧. In Colloquial Ainu, the second-person intransitive subject markers are *e-* for singular and *eci-* for plural, alongside *-es-*, which is unique to the Ishikari dialect ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-colloquial-ainu-the-second-person-intransitive-subject⟧. In the colloquial subjective conjugation of Class I verbs, the second-person singular is plain *e-* or honorific *a-*, and the second-person plural is plain *echi-* or honorific *a-* ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-the-colloquial-subjective-conjugation-of-class-i⟧. In spoken Hokkaido Ainu, the second-person singular object is marked by *e-* or honorific *i-*, and the second-person plural object is marked by *echi-* or honorific *i-* ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-the-spoken-language-the-second-person-singular⟧. Second-person subject markers always appear as prefixes regardless of whether the verb belongs to Class I or Class II, yielding the order 'object/complement + (subject-)verb' when the verb takes an object or complement ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--second-person-subject-markers-always-appear-as-prefixes⟧. Because of this syncretism, forms such as *e-kore* are ambiguous between 'you give him' (with a second-person singular subject and zero third-person object) and 'he/she gives you' (with a zero third-person subject and second-person singular object) ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--forms-like-e-kore-are-ambiguous-between-you⟧. In Classical Ainu, the second-person singular intransitive subject is marked by the prefix *e-* ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-classical-ainu-the-second-person-singular-intransitive⟧, the second-person singular transitive subject is marked by the prefix *e-* ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-classical-ainu-the-second-person-singular-transitive⟧, the second-person object markers are *e-* in the singular and *eci-* in the plural ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-classical-ainu-the-second-person-object-markers⟧, and the affixes *e-* (singular) and *eci-* (plural) thus mark both subject and object ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-classical-ainu-second-person-affixes-e-sg⟧. In the Shizunai dialect, both the nominative and objective cases of the second-person singular are marked by the prefix *e-* ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--shizunai-second-person-singular-e⟧. In the Saru dialect, the second-person singular pronoun is *'e'áni*, and the corresponding affix is *'e-* without distinction between nominative and objective case ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-second-person-singular-pronoun-in-the-saru⟧. This Saru second-person singular form *'e'áni* (*'e-*) is used for a single addressee, except when a woman addresses an adult male ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-second-person-singular-form-e-ni-e⟧. In Chitose Ainu, the second-person affixes *e-* (singular) and *eci-* (plural) are not purely neutral forms, but correspond to informal expressions like Japanese *omae(ra)* or *anta(ra)* ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-second-person-personal-affixes-e-singular-and⟧. In self-directed speech in the Chitose dialect, the second-person prefix *e=* can be used to refer to the narrator or speaker for vividness ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-self-directed-speech-the-second-person-prefix⟧, and more generally across Ainu, the second person is used when talking to oneself in monologue ⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-ainu-the-second-person-is-used-when⟧.
text.ja: 2人称単数主格の人称接辞は *e-* であり⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-second-person-singular-subjective-personal-affix-is⟧、2人称単数目的格の人称接辞も同様に *e-*（「お前を」「お前に」）である⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-second-person-singular-objective-personal-affix-is⟧⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-second-person-singular-objective-person-affix-is⟧。2人称接辞には主格と目的格の形態的区別がなく、単数は *e-*、複数は *eci-* が主語と目的語の双方で用いられる⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--second-person-affixes-have-no-morphological-distinction-between⟧。口語アイヌ語において、2人称自動詞主語標識は単数で *e-*、複数で *eci-* であり、石狩方言特有の接尾辞として *-es-* が存在する⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-colloquial-ainu-the-second-person-intransitive-subject⟧。第I類動詞の口語主格活用において、2人称単数は普通形が *e-*、敬称が *a-* であり、2人称複数は普通形が *echi-*、敬称が *a-* である⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-the-colloquial-subjective-conjugation-of-class-i⟧。北海道の口語において、2人称単数目的格は *e-* または敬称の *i-*、2人称複数目的格は *echi-* または敬称の *i-* で標示される⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-the-spoken-language-the-second-person-singular⟧。2人称主語標識は動詞が第I類であるか第II類であるかを問わず常に接頭辞として現れ、目的語または補語をとる場合の語順は「目的語／補語＋（主語-）動詞」となる⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--second-person-subject-markers-always-appear-as-prefixes⟧。この同形性のため、*e-kore* のような形式は「あなたが彼に与える」（2人称単数主語、3人称ゼロ目的語）と「彼/彼女があなたに与える」（3人称ゼロ主語、2人称単数目的語）の間で曖昧である⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--forms-like-e-kore-are-ambiguous-between-you⟧。古典アイヌ語において、2人称単数自動詞主語は接頭辞 *e-* で標示され⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-classical-ainu-the-second-person-singular-intransitive⟧、2人称単数他動詞主語も接頭辞 *e-* で標示され⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-classical-ainu-the-second-person-singular-transitive⟧、2人称目的語標識は単数で *e-*、複数で *eci-* であり⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-classical-ainu-the-second-person-object-markers⟧、接辞 *e-*（単数）および *eci-*（複数）が主語と目的語の双方を標示する⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-classical-ainu-second-person-affixes-e-sg⟧。静内方言において、2人称単数の主格および目的格はともに接頭辞 *e-* によって標示される⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--shizunai-second-person-singular-e⟧。沙流方言の2人称単数代名詞は *'e'áni* であり、対応する接辞は主格・目的格の区別なく *'e-* である⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-second-person-singular-pronoun-in-the-saru⟧。この沙流方言の2人称単数形式 *'e'áni* (*'e-*) は相手1人に対して用いられるが、女性が成人の男性に向かって言う場合を除く⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-second-person-singular-form-e-ni-e⟧。千歳アイヌ語において、2人称接辞 *e-*（単数）および *eci-*（複数）は純粋に中立的な形式ではなく、日本語の「お前(ら)」「あんた(ら)」のようなくだけた言い方に相当する⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--the-second-person-personal-affixes-e-singular-and⟧。千歳方言の自問自答の場面において、臨場感を出すために叙述者自身を指して2人称の *e=* が用いられることがあり⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-self-directed-speech-the-second-person-prefix⟧、アイヌ語一般においても独り言を言う場合に2人称が用いられる⟦claim:person/first-second-person-singular-affixes--in-ainu-the-second-person-is-used-when⟧。
